newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods-Gasoline diffs hold their ground.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods-Gasoline diffs hold their ground.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product differentials held much of their strength Tuesday in a market showing little news or solid signs of when output would resume at two major refineries.

In New York Harbor traders were awaiting word that Tosco's New Jersey cracker had resumed production. In the Gulf Coast it remained unclear for how long Exxon's cracker in Baytown, Texas, would remain down.
Little news also subdued NYMEX, where September gasoline was up 1.36 cent at 66.80 cents a gallon and September heating was up 0.56 cent at 55.65 cents a gallon.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Gasoline values held their ground Tuesday morning though buyers, like on Monday, stayed away from the market in the hopes that the market will cool down off its highs before they absolutely have to close deals.
"It's still pretty tight up front," said one trader, though he was surprised the "M2" regular conventional grade was holding so much of its value relative to the "A2" regular reformulated blend.

A small piece of prompt A2 for delivery into the Buckeye Pipeline was heard done late Monday evening at 9.25 cents over September NYMEX, though the broader prompt market remained valued at 9.00 cents over.
Prompt M2 was meanwhile offered at 6.50 cents over September futures, but bids were nowhere to be seen.

In highly topical piece of gossip, one trader said he had heard Tosco was offering any month A2, which was pegged at 6.00 cents over. But others doubted the talk, saying Tosco does not sell much material on the spot market to begin with.

Tosco is said to have successfully restarted its huge fluid catalytic cracking unit at its Bayway refinery in New Jersey over the weekend following maintenance after an unexpected shutdown about three weeks ago.
U.S. GULF

The U.S. Gulf markets were relatively quiet Tuesday morning in a day that so far had little news. Some short covering by an independent trading house continued to put pressure on the front 24th cycle of M1 conventional unleaded, which had a scheduling deadline in Pasadena and Port Arthur, Texas, on Monday.
The trading house apparently bought 25,000 barrels of M1 for -0.10 cent under the September print, players said.
Prompt M1 unleaded conventional, now the back 24th cycle with a scheduling deadline on August 21st, was pegged at -2.25/-2.00 cents below the print. A -2.25 cent deal was done.
"There is not that much activity," said a Gulf trader.

Reformulated regular gasoline differentials, or A1, were pegged slightly weaker at 3.25/3.75 cents over September futures. Reformulated premium gasoline, or D1, was notional at Monday's level of 7.00/8.00 cents over the September NYMEX.
Prompt barrels of V1-grade, or premium unleaded gasoline, were done at 6.50 cents and 6.60 cents over the print, about steady with Monday. The V1-grade schedules today.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent unleaded gasoline was notionally steady in the Group Three, although Chicago was heard up a tad at 0.50/0.75 cents over the print.
More buyers than sellers, however, continued to keep the market nervous that differentials were come off further in the week, particularly due to the return of good supply in the region.
Low sulphur diesel was also steady amid a lack of demand.
((--New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1620--))
